title: Girl Scouts: More than cookie sellers
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history and structure of the Girl Scouts: founder Juliette Gordon Low's 1912 founding of the first troop in Savannah, the age-based program levels (Daisies, Brownies, Juniors, Girl Scouts/Cadettes), the Girl Scout Law and badges, outdoor and STEM activities, inclusivity and desegregation, and the history and business of Girl Scout cookies, including the cookie varieties, councils, and Saul Bass's trefoil logo. The episode also includes a Kiva team listener-mail plug and a guest-friend segment featuring Annabella, a junior Girl Scout.
topics: Girl Scout levels Daisies Brownies Juniors

segments.title: Opening banter and childhood scouting memories
segments.summary: The hosts open the show, joke about whether Jerry was a Girl Scout, and cite membership statistics (about one in three American adult women were Girl Scouts). They swap stories about their own short-lived cub scouting and nephew Noah's Eagle Scout run.

segments.title: Dues and shout-outs to real Girl Scout troops
segments.summary: They note the low annual dues of about twenty-five dollars and credit cookie sales for funding. They read remarks from Annabella, a junior Girl Scout, about entrepreneurship, cookie sales, and community impact, and give shout-outs to Troop 1107 and a troop led by a friend.

segments.title: Inclusivity and Juliette Gordon Low's early life
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Girl Scouts' long record of inclusivity, including desegregation in the 1950s and the inclusion of girls with disabilities. They then introduce founder Juliette Gordon Low of Savannah, Georgia, describing her troubled marriage and her meeting with Robert Baden-Powell in London.

segments.title: Founding of the first troop and program levels
segments.summary: Low starts the first American troop in March 1912 with eighteen girls, including her niece Daisy Gordon. The hosts go through the age-based levels, from Daisies (five to six) through Brownies, Juniors, and the Girl Scouts group for ages eleven to seventeen, plus the Girl Scout Law pedals and the ceremony of the dime.

segments.title: Badges, STEM, service projects, and outdoor activities
segments.summary: The hosts describe how girls earn badges through crafts, service projects, and STEM activities such as coding. They cover the emphasis on camping, the outdoors, and s'mores, and mention the early Girl Scout handbook recipe for s'mores.

segments.title: Juliettes, councils, troops, and male leaders
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Girl Scouts are organized into roughly 130 councils that split into troops, and describe Juliettes, who are solo members who can earn badges with an adult mentor. They also note that men can serve as Girl Scout leaders, with a female co-leader.

segments.title: Girl Scout cookies: history, varieties, and sales
segments.summary: The hosts trace Girl Scout cookies to a 1917 Muskogee, Oklahoma troop and the 1922 recipe in The American Girl. They discuss popular varieties (Thin Mints, Samoas, Tagalongs, Do-Si-Dos, Trefoils), the difference between Samoas and Caramel deLites, and discontinued flavors such as Apple Cinnamons and Savannah Smiles.

segments.title: Cookie money, badges, and the trefoil logo
segments.summary: The hosts explain that most cookie revenue stays with local councils, with about 12 to 17 percent going to troops, and that cookie badges reward goal-setting rather than sales volume. They describe Saul Bass's 1979 trefoil logo and its three girls.

segments.title: Politics, controversy, and religion in Girl Scouts
segments.summary: The hosts discuss criticism of the Girl Scouts as feminist or politically motivated, Betty Friedan's board role, support for Title IX, and the optional religious wording of the Girl Scout promise. They also list famous former Girl Scouts.

segments.title: Kiva team plug and listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts plug the show's Kiva microlending team, started in 2009, which has loaned almost nine point three million dollars, and encourage listeners to join. They read a listener email from Lee Rondorf in Minnesota asking for the plug again.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and give the show's contact address.
